analysis: The trial completed successfully but regressed: host validation macro HR@10 was 0.5763 versus the prior 0.595, a decrease of 0.0187. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.635, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.605, Electronics 0.415, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.650. Electronics improved from the reported prior 0.405, but the overall result does not support replacing the previous objective with this 16-negative sampled-softmax configuration. The objective changes candidate competition and gradient scaling; the available results do not establish why performance declined. Separate expert metrics were not supplied, so the regression cannot be attributed conclusively to SASRec alone. Training consumed 2,037.63 GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Retained independent per-category LightGCN and SASRec experts with equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion using constant 60. LightGCN uses learned weights over three propagation depths, item biases, recency-weighted history profiles, target-excluded training profiles, and 32-negative sampled softmax. SASRec retains two causal attention blocks, 50-dimensional embeddings, maximum sequence length 50, and dropout 0.2. Its training now gathers active transitions and applies temperature-1 cross-entropy over one positive and 16 uniformly sampled unseen negatives with replacement. Architecture, inference scoring, checkpoint loading, predictor generation, all four dataset routes, and seed-42 training remain preserved. Added deterministic sampling, loss, gradient, and export-parity fixtures.
